'''Victor Bangert''' (born 28 November 1950) is Professor of [[Mathematics]] at the Mathematisches Institut in [[Freiburg]], [[Germany]]. His main interests are [[differential geometry]] and [[dynamical systems theory]]. He specialises in the theory of [[closed geodesic]]s, wherein one of his significant results, combined with another one due to [http://www.math.northwestern.edu/people/faculty/john-franks.html John Franks], implies that every [[Riemannian manifold|Riemannian]] 2-sphere possesses infinitely many closed geodesics. He also made important contributions to [[Aubry–Mather theory]].

He obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from [[Universität Dortmund]] in 1977 under the supervision of [[Rolf Wilhelm Walter]], with the thesis ''Konvexität in riemannschen Mannigfaltigkeiten''.<ref name="MGP">{{MathGenealogy|id=28718|title=Victor Bangert}}</ref>

He served in the editorial board of "[https://link.springer.com/journal/229 manuscripta mathematica]" from 1996 to 2017.

Bangert was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the 1994 International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Zürich]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |title=International Mathematical Union (IMU) |publisher=Mathunion.org |access-date=15 May 2017 |archive-date=24 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>
